about: What the licence gate (tools/license/gate.mjs) holds the repository to: the licences a dependency may come under, the names of other owners that may not be used, and where every picture, packed file and third-party directory came from. A change here is a decision about what the product may contain, so it is made in a pull request of its own words, with the reason written beside it. The gate checks what a machine can check; it is not a legal opinion (docs/ip-audit.md says what is left for counsel).

licences.why: Licences that let the product be sold closed, with no duty beyond keeping the notice and the text: the permissive family. Anything with a share-alike duty (the GPL family, AGPL, SSPL, EPL, CDDL, Creative Commons ShareAlike or NonCommercial) is absent on purpose, and so is anything unnamed.

MPL-2.0.why: File-level copyleft, allowed for these five by name and for nothing else. They come in through the Tauri stack (dirs for option-ext, dom_query for the Servo CSS crates), unmodified, and no file of theirs is copied into the repository; their source stays at crates.io. As commonly read, a closed program may link unchanged MPL files while their source stays available and their notices are kept; docs/ip-audit.md §3 asks counsel to confirm that reading for this product. A sixth crate under MPL-2.0 is a new decision, not a default.

marks.why: Names that belong to someone else and that the product must not use as its own or lean on. Platforms, hardware and tools the product runs on or speaks to are named plainly where a user needs them and credited in NOTICE.md (Third-party trademarks); those are not listed here.

listed.why: a film franchise's name for falling code
a film franchise's mark, which the terminal's first name held
a console maker's name the owner had taken out of the product; pads are named by their layout
another owner's name that came in with a pasted plan; the product's own names are original
another game's or film's title; the city is described in its own words, never by comparison
the language's name is never shortened

NOTICE.md.why: The notice that ships ends there; below it is research for counsel, which has to name the marks it weighs.

exempt.src/licenceGate.test.ts: The gate's own test, which shows the scan catching each kind of name.
exempt.src/compliance.test.ts: The page's older list, with examples.
exempt.docs/ip-audit.md: The audit for counsel, which has to name what was found and removed.

assets.why: Every picture, icon and packed data file in the repository, with where it came from and whose it is. `open` is a question only the owner can answer; the gate repeats it on every run until it is answered here.
